title: ASME BPVC Section VIII Division 1 internal-pressure thickness formulas and published worked examples
note: The Code is paywalled. Only the formulas (reproduced in many public sources) and third-party worked examples are used. Every expected value is re-derived from the formula in data/derive_expected.py; 'published' is what the source prints.

UG-27(c)(1).limits: t <= R/2 and P <= 0.385 S E

UG-27(c)(2).limits: applicability limits not confirmed by a fetched source (grade C) - not gated
UG-27(c)(2).use: longitudinal stress; reported, MVP gate on the formula only

UG-32 hemispherical.limits: applicability limits not confirmed by a fetched source (grade C) - not gated

UG-99(b) hydrostatic test.Pt: 1.3 * MAWP * (S_test / S_design), lowest ratio over the materials
UG-99(b) hydrostatic test.gradeReason: two independent extracts (engineersedge, API 510 formula sheet) agree

formulas.corroded dimensions: R and D in the corroded condition (R + CA, D + 2 CA); thickness available = t_nominal - CA (- mill undertolerance when given)

units: symbols as in the Code: P design pressure (gauge), R inside radius, D inside diameter, S allowable stress at design temperature, E joint efficiency, CA corrosion allowance

examples.source: S7 Codeware INSPECT API 510 sample report (search extract)
examples.gradeReason: published value + independent re-derivation agree to 4 printed digits

examples.source: S6 Hexagon CodeCalc help 'Example Shell Analysis' (search extract): TR = P (D/2 + CA) / (S E - 0.6 P)

examples.use: documents that sources differ on corroded radius; llull default = corroded (Code convention, as UG27-B), option corrodedDimensions:false reproduces this example

examples.gradeReason: published (truncated to 3 decimals) + re-derivation; formula confirmed by S9

materialAllowableNote: S for SA-516 Gr 70 = 20 000 psi (137.9 MPa) is used by the PVE CodeCalc reports [S14]; it is a Section II Part D value (temperature dependent). llull never defaults S: it is an input, or read from a material record with a source; otherwise EQP_ALLOWABLE_MISSING.
